crime: For weeks, {WITCH_NAME} let her pinhole star cards go in the lounge, and each one dropped at her feet. No one here would treasure them.

Then one girl took to lying on the lake shore every clear evening, naming the stars. One night a card sailed out of the lounge and found her. Every night since, at nine, she caught one and pinned it above her bunk.

One afternoon in the courtyard, {WITCH_NAME} put a card into the girl's hand for the first time. It was pricked with her own faint constellation. The girl held it up to the light and laughed. "There's hardly anything there. Do me Orion again." She handed it back.

Once, at a classroom window, {WITCH_NAME} had held up a pinhole card of a faint constellation, and her classmates had laughed: "There's nothing there." Since then she had pricked only the stars other people name.

At eight that night, the girl left the lounge for the lake shore. {WITCH_NAME} stayed by the fireplace with the others. At nine, in front of them all, she let go of a black card. It dropped onto the rug at her feet, and the prisoner beside her set it on the mantel. Soon after, she went out. At the water's edge she knelt behind the girl and held her face under the starlit shallows until the girl stopped moving.
At dawn the prisoners found her face down in the shallows, with finger bruises on the back of her neck and, in her pocket, the card she had caught the night before she died.
"She was dead before nine," the court decided. "Her card found no one, and {WITCH_NAME} was sitting right here with us."

Then one prisoner held the fallen card up to the light. Not one pinhole let it through. A card with nothing on it falls no matter who is alive. {WITCH_NAME} had let it go so the girl at the lake would seem dead by nine, and then gone out to her.
fields.epitaph: The only card anyone ever believed was the one with nothing on it.
fields.epithet: Stars That Fall at Her Own Feet
execution: The execution stand raises a towering black card in the trial court, with her strapped upright across its face. A giant pin hangs poised before her chest.
The pin drives through her and through the card, then again, and again, point by point, tracing the faint constellation she loved.
Then the stand lets go of the card. It flies to no one. It tips forward and falls.
It lies flat at the foot of the stand, over her. Nothing beneath it moves, and no one lifts it.

magic.name: Homing Gift
magic.text: Anything she gives away flies from her hand to whoever will treasure it most.
